clue.text: Female bringing endless grief to boyfriend

indicators.note: endless says the word for grief loses its final letter

parts.note: woe means grief
a girl's man is her boyfriend

explanation.surface: A woman upsets her partner by causing him unending sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman is an adult human female.

clue.text: Room for improvement on gown in outfit

indicators.note: in a down clue, the gown placed on the room goes after it

parts.note: a hospital ward is a room where patients get better
a robe is a gown

explanation.surface: Someone needs a better gown within their outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of clothes, a whole outfit, is so called.

clue.text: Something that draws circle in small generator

parts.note: a magnet draws, attracts, metal
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: An attracting device ring inside a little dynamo.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small electrical generator using permanent magnets, as for ignition.

clue.text: Flower out of line

indicators.note: out of order, so the letters of line are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bloom sticks out of a straight row.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is something that flows, a crossword name for a river; this is Egypt's great river.

clue.text: A cryptographer's ruse of simply taking initial characters

definitions.text: A cryptographer's ruse of simply taking initial characters

parts.words: A cryptographer's ruse of simply taking initial characters
parts.note: describes a piece of writing whose message is spelt by the opening letters of its lines

explanation.definitionFit: In this kind of verse the first letter of each line spells out a hidden word, a simple code.

clue.text: Obstetrician's terms?

parts.note: a baby doctor's terms would be payment when the baby is born

explanation.definitionFit: A trade arrangement where payment is made when goods arrive.

clue.text: No ground for a square cut?

definitions.text: No ground for a square cut?

parts.words: No ground for a square cut?
parts.note: a cricket shot called the square cut, but here a shape that is not square, and also a London cricket ground

explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; the square cut is a cricket stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded elongated shape is no square; the word also names a famous cricket venue.

clue.text: This great storm split a party

parts.note: torn means split
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A big storm broke up a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm is a great storm.

clue.text: Yachting centre we found in Greek island

indicators.note: found in means the word we sits inside the island

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A sailing resort we discovered on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight town hosts the famous annual regatta, Cowes Week.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Wight port is famous for its annual sailing regatta.

clue.text: Last chance to prepare for the night?

definitions.text: Last chance to prepare for the night?

parts.words: Last chance to prepare for the night?
parts.note: sounds like getting ready for bed, but means the final full rehearsal before the first night of a show

explanation.definitionFit: The final full run-through in costume before a play's opening night.

clue.text: Gunners with automatic pistol returning every day, we hear

indicators.note: returning tells us the gunners and the pistol are read back to front together

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
the Luger is a German automatic pistol

explanation.surface: Soldiers come back daily carrying their sidearms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns RALUGER round. The definition says 'every day' sounds like 'everyday', the adjective meaning ordinary or usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everyday is normal, habitual and routine.

clue.text: Line on stout pole for a bird

indicators.note: in an across clue, a line placed on the pole follows it

parts.note: a spar is a thick pole, as on a ship's rigging
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A line rigged on a ship's pole provides a perch for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small brown songbird, common in towns.

clue.text: Regrets French ways?

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry about the way the French do things.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret is to be sorry about something; in French streets are called by this word.

clue.text: First capital gains tax in Berkshire

parts.note: the capital letter that comes first in the alphabet
scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: A capital gains tax applied first in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital gains tax' looks like one phrase, but split it: 'First capital' is A, 'gains' is a link and 'tax' is SCOT. The definition names a place found in Berkshire, an English county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse town of royal race-meeting fame lies in Berkshire.

clue.text: Get through canyon

explanation.surface: Someone makes it through a gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: To get through an exam is to succeed; a mountain gap or gorge route is another sense.

clue.text: The French hail-and-farewell

parts.note: le is French for the
ave is Latin for hail

explanation.surface: A French greeting that is also goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: To take one's leave is to say farewell; the noun means a parting.

clue.text: Stays make pimples come up

indicators.note: in a down clue, come up means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: spots are pimples

explanation.surface: Wearing corsets brings out spots.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to halt or remain; as a verb, it means stays.

clue.text: Cruelly raided in Bogota-breaking down, naturally!

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the following letters are roughly treated and reshaped

explanation.surface: A raid in Colombia's capital wrecks things, as nature would.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural decomposition by bacteria and other organisms is breaking down naturally.

clue.text: Range of vision about eight, yes?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Is the extent of one's view roughly eight?
explanation.definitionFit: Sight, the ability to see, gives a range of vision.

clue.text: Game to promote Old Meg on the board

parts.note: to shove is to push forward, promote
meg was old slang for a halfpenny, a former British coin

explanation.surface: A game in which old coins are pushed up a board.
explanation.walkthrough: A halfpenny was an old British coin worth half a penny, nicknamed a meg; 'on the board' describes how the pub game is played.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British pub game in which coins are pushed along a marked board.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman concealed gaol-break

parts.note: hid means concealed

indicators.note: break means the letters of the prison word are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman hid during a prison escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the minor nobility in Spain was a gentleman of this rank.

clue.text: Well-versed in New Latin of the wedding ceremony

indicators.note: in places the knowledgeable word inside the reworked letters
new suggests the letters of Latin are formed afresh

parts.note: up as in well up on, knowledgeable

explanation.surface: Knowledgeable in modern Latin for a marriage service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-versed' is UP as in 'well up on'; 'New' makes NTIAL from the Latin letters, and 'in' puts UP just after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes matters relating to marriage or a wedding.

clue.text: Fellow notices such fashions

parts.note: ads are notices or advertisements

explanation.surface: A man sees the latest trends.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-lived crazes are passing fashions.

clue.text: Father falls behind and peters out

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for father
lags means falls behind

explanation.surface: Dad trails behind and runs out of steam.
explanation.definitionFit: To weaken and fade is to tire, to peter out.

clue.text: Poor excuse for a round of applause

explanation.surface: A feeble pretext is met with clapping.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense is an evasive excuse or saving clause; a burst of cheering or clapping is another.

clue.text: Nothing the matter with this musical composition

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
pus is matter from a wound

explanation.surface: There is no problem with this piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbered work by a composer is so labelled.

clue.text: Dismal doctor treated with tar

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, AB being an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A gloomy doctor dealt with a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull, dreary colourless thing is dismal.

clue.text: The laundry-bay?

explanation.surface: The laundry room by the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large bay on the east coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A load of clothes to be cleaned is laundry; the Lincolnshire inlet is a bay.

clue.text: Laurel's very funny in these attractions

indicators.note: very funny means comically distorted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stan Laurel's comedy is the appeal of these films.
explanation.definitionFit: Charms and enticements are attractions.

clue.text: Version of R1?

explanation.surface: Is this a variant of a radio station?
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs of basic schooling are reading, writing and arithmetic; R1 is the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An interpretation or rendering is a version; the first of the three Rs is literacy's first skill.

clue.text: Footwear account of an African wader

parts.note: a shoe is footwear
a bill is an account

explanation.surface: A shoe invoice gives an account of an African wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large stork-like bird of African swamps with a huge clog-shaped beak.

clue.text: He made notes on movements of planets, we hear

definitions.text: He made notes on movements of planets, we hear

parts.words: He made notes on movements of planets, we hear
parts.note: reads like an astronomer, but means a composer whose suite in movements is named after the planets, music we listen to

explanation.definitionFit: Gustav, the English composer, wrote The Planets suite.
